name: MetLife
description: MetLife sells insurance and retirement products mostly to employers and institutions rather than to individuals in the US. Group Benefits sells life, dental, disability and related cover to employers; Retirement and Income Solutions takes over corporate pension obligations and sells stable-value and funding-agreement products; Asia, Latin America and EMEA sell life, accident and health and savings products through agents, banks and partners. In late 2025 it made MetLife Investment Management (MIM), an institutional asset manager that bought PineBridge Investments for $885 million (preliminary), a reportable segment. Profit is premiums and fees less claims and expenses plus the spread earned on the investment portfolio. Adjusted earnings were $5.9 billion in 2025.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6311 (Life Insurance). The biggest line is US employer group benefits (44% of adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues), followed by pension risk transfers and institutional products (RIS, 21%), then Asia, Latin America and EMEA, plus a small institutional asset manager (MIM).

businessLines.name: Retirement & Income Solutions (RIS)
businessLines.how: A plan sponsor or investor hands MetLife a lump sum (single premium) and MetLife earns the spread between what its investments earn and what it pays out or credits; PRT deals are lumpy one-time premiums that then produce decades of spread.
businessLines.description: US funding and financing products for institutions: pension risk transfer annuities (single-premium buyouts and buy-ins), stable value GICs, funding agreements, institutional income annuities, structured settlements.
